text: Spatial and optimization controls for masked temporal pretraining in forest clear cut classification
Mehmet Oğuz Güneren¹ and Nida Kumbasar²
¹ Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering, Istanbul Technical University, Istanbul, Türkiye (gnrnoguz@gmail.com)
² TÜBİTAK BİLGEM, Information Technologies Institute (BTE), Data Valorization Department, Gebze, Kocaeli, Türkiye (nida.kumbasar@tubitak.gov.tr)
Draft for co-author review • 18 October 2026 • Version paper_v4 with declared extensions paper_v5 (grouping radius) and paper_v6 (label-budget curve)
Abstract

Self-supervised pretraining may improve satellite time-series classification when labels are scarce, but comparisons can confound its objective with additional optimization. We examine this issue using 2,213 high-confidence DISFOR Sentinel-2 series, comprising 1,937 stable-forest and 276 clear-cut locations. A fixed protocol evaluates random forests, temporal convolutional networks, supervised Transformers and masked-reconstruction Transformers with five spatially grouped folds, three training seeds and two label budgets. Spatial components connect locations within 5 km and shared source disturbance events. All 180 fits are retained. At 20% labels, block-and-band pretraining achieves pooled out-of-fold macro-F1 0.8690, compared with 0.8322 for a 40-epoch supervised Transformer; the paired difference is 0.0368 (conditional spatial-component bootstrap 95% interval [0.0245, 0.0506]). However, a supervised control approximately matching the total optimizer-step budget reaches 0.8987. Independent-cell masking reaches 0.8609, and the corresponding masking comparison does not clearly separate the methods. With all labels, the CNN reaches 0.9299 and the pretrained Transformer 0.9287. Two declared extensions qualify this picture. A label-budget curve at 5%, 10% and 50% labels on the identical folds and seeds shows that below 20% labels the pretrained Transformer trails the step-matched Transformer, the CNN and even the random forest, so its benefit is confined to the short-training comparison; at 50% labels the neural recipes converge. A single-seed grouping-radius analysis at 5, 10 and 20 km shows that the step-matched advantage does not persist under coarser spatial separation, where the pretrained model degrades least. Metadata and missingness controls expose residual sampling information. This is a retrospective audit of recipes developed on the same dataset, not untouched external validation. An unused-location support audit yields only one positive among 111 eligible windows and is therefore not scored. These results support optimization-aware, spatially structured evaluation rather than a general claim of self-supervised superiority.
Keywords: Earth observation; Sentinel-2; forest disturbance; self-supervised learning; spatial validation; optimization controls
1 Introduction

Dense satellite time series offer observations of vegetation before and after disturbance, whereas reliable event labels remain costly to obtain. Self-supervised learning can use observations without their class labels before supervised adaptation. This motivates a practical question: when a pretrained classifier improves under a limited label budget, how much of that improvement survives a stronger supervised comparator? A useful answer requires both geographically separated evaluation and explicit control of additional training.

Masked representation learning for multivariate time series is established prior work [3]. In Earth observation, lightweight pretrained temporal models such as Presto already demonstrate the broader relevance of time-series pretraining [7]. Zhang et al. study a distinct forest-disturbance setting with Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2, irregular temporal modeling and self-supervision [2]. Resampling-based contrastive augmentation has also been examined for remote-sensing sequences [8]. These studies motivate the present questions; their datasets, objectives and metrics are not directly comparable to this experiment. We neither reproduce those systems nor claim a new Transformer architecture or a state-of-the-art result.

Forest disturbance mapping from optical time series has a long record, from global Landsat-based cover-change products [17] and continuous change detection [20] to European disturbance regime maps [18] and reviews of optical disturbance and degradation methods [19]; a recent global disturbance-type dataset extends this line [24]. Deep sequence models for satellite image time series include temporal convolutions [11], self-attention over raw optical sequences [12] and pixel-set temporal attention encoders [13]. Self-supervised pretraining for such sequences has followed the masked-token recipe of language and vision models [14], with SITS-BERT [9], SITS-Former [10], SatMAE [15], Presto [7] and generalist geospatial foundation models [16] as representative examples; multimodal Sentinel-1/2 fusion is also common in the applied literature [25, 26]. The methodological concern that motivates our design is that random cross-validation can overstate map accuracy under spatial dependence [4, 21, 22], although the appropriate design depends on the intended inference target [23].

We use a restricted binary subset of DISFOR, a public European disturbance time-series resource [1]. Structured dependence can compromise ordinary cross-validation, making spatial and event grouping relevant [4]. Yet spatial separation alone does not resolve training-budget imbalance, missingness cues or dataset-specific model development. Our contribution is a reproducible empirical audit that reports these issues together: paired label subsets, fixed training recipes, an optimization-step control, a masking control, covariate-only diagnostics and an explicit audit of unused evaluation support. The central comparison was fixed before the new cross-fit scores were computed; the architecture choices had already been explored on this dataset.
2 Data and study design

We pin JR-DIGITAL/DISFOR to revision 2562332e35c94c2339aeb341ffaed2a99faae7d6. The downloaded sample table contains 3,822 locations; an upstream dataset-card count of 3,823 is not used. DISFOR provides interpreted labels and Sentinel-2 observations, with source campaigns involving disturbance polygons, sampling strata and storm-event information. The dataset article is an ESSD Discussions preprint under review at the time of this draft [1]. The labels are existing human interpretations and supporting source information, not newly collected field measurements.

We retain high-confidence locations and construct one 24-month calendar window per location. The first year must be labeled stable forest. A positive window has an eligible clear-cut event in its second year; a negative remains stable through both years. Target years range from 2018 to 2023. Candidate event windows are prioritized deterministically, and stable-window selection follows the fixed sample-identifier rule in the preprocessing code. This is retrospective classification of curated windows, not event-onset forecasting or complete landscape mapping. Event dates guide dataset construction but are not input features.

The ten channels are B02, B03, B04, B05, B06, B07, B08, B8A, B11 and B12. Within each month, we take the median of source-clear observations whose scene-classification values are 4 or 5. Each retained window has at least six observed months in each year. Missing values retain a Boolean mask; no temporal interpolation is applied. Values use the source-provided digital-number scale without an added radiometric offset. Per-channel means and standard deviations use observed values from the outer-training partition only. Time features encode elapsed days and an annual sine/cosine cycle on monthly calendar slots. Figure 1 shows retained locations and observed-month support.

text: 3 Models and experimental controls

The primary methods are a random forest, a temporal CNN, a supervised Transformer and the same Transformer with masked-reconstruction pretraining. The random forest [5] has 500 trees, minimum leaf size 4, max_features=0.7 and balanced_subsample class weights. Its 60 features comprise per-channel observed mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, second-year minus first-year mean and observed fraction. It is therefore a temporal-summary baseline rather than a spatial image classifier.

Neural inputs concatenate ten normalized values, ten observation indicators and three time features. A linear projection precedes the encoder. The CNN has width 64 and three residual blocks with dilations 1, 2 and 4, each containing two width-three convolutions and group normalization. The Transformer has width 48, two encoder layers, four attention heads and feed-forward width 144. Both use GELU activations and an observed-time mean-pooling classifier. Entirely unobserved Transformer keys are masked. CNN dropout is 0.20; Transformer dropout is 0.15. The reconstruction head maps encoded slots to ten channel values.

Primary neural fits use 40 supervised epochs, batch size 64 and AdamW with weight decay 0.01. Learning rates are 0.001 for the CNN and 0.0005 for the Transformer. Cross-entropy uses inverse-frequency weights calculated from the labeled training subset, label smoothing 0.02 and gradient clipping at norm 1. Training randomly removes months with probability 0.10, restoring the original mask if removal would hide every observation. No early stopping, validation-based calibration, model selection or threshold fitting occurs within the new audit. All class decisions use probability 0.5. Reporting a Brier score does not imply a calibrated deployment model [6].

Masked pretraining uses all outer-training sequences, without using their class labels in the reconstruction loss, for 60 epochs at learning rate 0.001. Each series hides a contiguous block of two to six months plus two randomly selected complete bands. The loss is Smooth L1 over artificially hidden, originally observed cells. Naturally missing cells are not reconstruction targets. A safeguard retains visible and hidden support. On a fully observed 24-by-10 grid, nominal expected coverage is one third; boundary effects and actual missingness mean that observed-cell coverage need not equal one third for every series. After pretraining, the classifier is restored to its paired initial state, and supervised randomization is reset identically across paired methods.

For each seed (7, 17 or 27), labels are sampled in a nested random order separately within each class, using the ceiling of either 20% or 100% of the training class count. All methods and controls share these exact point identifiers. Because allocation uses known class membership, this is a controlled label-scarcity simulation, not a prospective annotation-cost experiment. Even supervised baselines may use all outer-training observations to estimate normalization; only the designated labeled subset enters classification loss. Held-out features are not used in normalization, pretraining or supervised fitting.

Four controls are run at 20% labels. First, independent-cell SSL masks each observed cell with probability one third, with support safeguards; this matches nominal masking scale, not every realized missing-data pattern. Second, a supervised Transformer receives enough epochs to approximately match SSL pretraining plus fine-tuning optimizer updates. Specifically, E = ceil((60 ceil(Ntrain/64) + 40 ceil(Nlabeled/64)) / ceil(Nlabeled/64)). This yields 320 epochs in all five folds. The control matches update counts within one labeled epoch, not floating-point operations, wall time, number of labeled presentations or objective. Third, a random forest uses only the 240 observation-mask entries. Fourth, another uses longitude, latitude, target year and numeric campaign index. Both diagnostic forests use the primary forest settings and the same labeled subsets.

The full design contains 5 folds × 3 seeds × 2 label budgets × 4 primary methods = 120 fits, plus 5 × 3 × 4 controls = 60 fits. All 180 completed fits, including weaker results, are retained. The protocol, code and processed-data hashes were frozen before these scores were produced. Earlier work on the same dataset informed the model recipes, so this audit is retrospective and is not nested, externally preregistered or free of dataset-level adaptive selection.
4 Outcomes and uncertainty

The primary endpoint is the block-and-band SSL minus 40-epoch supervised Transformer difference in macro-F1 at 20% labels. For each method and seed, we pool the five held-out folds into 2,213 predictions and compute metrics once. We then report the mean and sample standard deviation across the three seeds. We do not treat the fifteen fold-by-seed scores as fifteen independent observations. Average precision is labeled AP in the tables; it is the stepwise precision-recall summary returned by average_precision_score, not trapezoidal PR area. We also retain ROC-AUC, clear-cut recall, Brier score and confusion matrices.

A paired cluster bootstrap resamples the 874 spatial components with replacement 2,000 times. Each draw applies identical component multiplicities to both methods and keeps all three seed predictions together; its statistic is the mean of the three paired pooled macro-F1 differences. Percentile 2.5% and 97.5% bounds are reported. No draw lacked either class. These are conditional intervals for the existing cohort, folds and trained predictions. They do not include uncertainty from adaptive recipe development or refitting on new training samples. Secondary comparisons are exploratory and not multiplicity-adjusted tests.
5 Results

Figure 2 and Table 3 summarize the primary comparisons. At 20% labels, masked pretraining improves macro-F1 from 0.8322 to 0.8690, a difference of 0.0368 with conditional 95% interval [0.0245, 0.0506]. The CNN reaches 0.8721, slightly above SSL, while the random forest reaches 0.8452. The SSL-versus-CNN interval [-0.0194, 0.0125] spans zero. With all labels, the three neural recipes have mean macro-F1 between 0.9285 and 0.9299; the small numerical differences do not establish a generally best architecture.

caption: Table 3. Primary pooled out-of-fold results. SD is across three seeds, not a confidence interval.

text: The optimization control changes the interpretation (Figure 3 and Table 4). The step-matched supervised Transformer reaches macro-F1 0.8987, exceeding SSL by 0.0297; the SSL-minus-control interval is [-0.0430, -0.0179]. Consequently, the main short-training comparison cannot be read as evidence that reconstruction is superior to spending more supervised optimization steps. SSL still has higher AP (0.8636 versus 0.8445), whereas the control has lower Brier score (0.0417 versus 0.0492). Thresholded discrimination, ranking and probability error therefore favor different aspects of the predictions.

Independent-cell SSL reaches 0.8609. The block-and-band advantage is 0.0080, with interval [-0.0013, 0.0178]; these data do not establish that the structured mask is reliably better. The observation-mask-only and metadata-only controls reach macro-F1 0.5515 and 0.6455, respectively. Their AP values are 0.1738 and 0.3979, above the retained positive prevalence of 0.1247 as a descriptive no-skill reference. These diagnostics indicate that missingness and sampling context contain predictive information; they do not measure a causal shortcut contribution to the spectral models.

text: An additional support audit searches high-confidence unused locations for eligible 2017 or 2024 windows. It excludes every previously used location, candidates within 5 km of used locations and shared source-event identifiers. Only 111 windows remain: 110 stable forest and one clear-cut. The nearest retained candidate is 5.0757 km from a previously used location. No classifier scores are computed on this probe because its positive support is inadequate for a credible clear-cut assessment. Moreover, unused points from DISFOR would remain same-source evaluation, not independent field validation.
5.1 Label-budget curve (declared extension paper_v6)

The original research plan listed label budgets below 20%, which paper_v4 did not run. A separate declared protocol (experiments/paper_v6_label_curve) therefore adds 5%, 10% and 50% budgets on the identical five folds, three seeds, nested label-allocation rule, recipes and 0.5 threshold, giving 225 additional fits. At 5% labels the labeled training set contains 89–90 locations, of which about one in eight is a clear cut, so single-seed values are intrinsically noisy. Table 5 and Figure 4 place the new budgets on one curve with the frozen 20% and 100% results. The SSL-minus-short-Transformer difference is 0.0618 at 5% (interval [0.0387, 0.0843]), 0.0309 at 10% ([0.0161, 0.0459]) and 0.0042 at 50% ([-0.0087, 0.0179]). Against the step-matched control the differences are -0.1124 ([-0.1334, -0.0919]), -0.0606 ([-0.0796, -0.0424]) and -0.0150 ([-0.0288, -0.0020]). The random forest reaches 0.8192 at 5% labels and 0.8362 at 10%; the CNN reaches 0.7946 and 0.8480. At the two lowest budgets, therefore, every stronger comparator, including the temporal-summary random forest, exceeds the pretrained Transformer (0.6955 and 0.7979), and the SSL advantage exists only relative to the 40-epoch Transformer. At 50% labels the four neural recipes lie within 0.02 of each other and the SSL-minus-short-Transformer interval covers zero.

caption: Table 5. Label-budget curve: pooled out-of-fold macro-F1 (mean ± SD over three seeds). Budgets 20% and 100% are the frozen paper_v4 fits; 5%, 10% and 50% are the declared paper_v6 fits on the same folds and seeds.

text: The extension was trained on different hardware from paper_v4 (recorded in experiments/paper_v6_label_curve/execution.json); recipes, seeds and label identifiers are identical, so results are comparable up to platform-level floating-point differences. Intervals at 5% and 10% are wide because few clear-cut components are labeled; they are conditional on the fixed cohort and are not multiplicity-adjusted.
5.2 Grouping-radius sensitivity (declared extension paper_v5)

The primary audit fixes a 5 km grouping radius. A separate single-seed extension (experiments/paper_v5_exploratory, seed 7, 20% labels, 75 fits) regroups the identical cohort at 5, 10 and 20 km and refits all five recipes on the induced folds. Coarser radii merge nearby components: 874 components at 5 km become 205 at 10 km and 54 at 20 km, and at 20 km some held-out folds contain only two clear-cut components. Table 6 and Figure 5 show that the ranking is not stable across radii. At 5 km the step-matched Transformer leads (0.9017 versus SSL 0.8726), at 10 km SSL and the control are close (0.8515 versus 0.8429), and at 20 km SSL is the strongest recipe (0.8437 versus 0.8216 for the control and 0.7997 for the CNN). The 5 km seed-7 fits reproduce the paper_v4 probabilities to within 2.2e-16.

caption: Table 6. Grouping-radius sensitivity at 20% labels, seed 7 only. Each value is one pooled out-of-fold macro-F1 over 2,213 locations; no seed SD or interval is available.

text: Because radius, fold membership and the labeled subset change together, this is a descriptive sensitivity analysis, not an estimate of a causal radius effect. It nevertheless indicates that the step-matched advantage reported in Section 5 is specific to the 5 km design and that the pretrained representation degrades less when training and test regions are separated more aggressively. Confirming this pattern would require additional seeds and, ideally, held-out regions defined independently of the sampling campaigns.
6 Discussion

The strongest result is a qualification of the initial low-label SSL improvement. Relative to a short supervised fit, reconstruction pretraining improves macro-F1 with a positive conditional interval. Relative to a much longer supervised fit, it does not. The experiment therefore identifies optimization budget as a material comparator choice. It does not prove that extra optimization is the sole mechanism: reconstruction and supervised objectives expose the model to different information, use different learning rates and induce different optimization trajectories. A complete causal decomposition would require additional controlled schedules and multiple independent datasets.

Mask structure is similarly unresolved. Block-and-band pretraining provides a plausible way to remove coherent temporal and spectral information, but the present interval includes no advantage over independent-cell masking. A proposal that treats this mask design itself as a demonstrated methodological innovation would overstate the evidence. The study is more defensible as an empirical investigation of when an apparent low-label benefit survives stronger controls.

The mask and metadata diagnostics matter because the sample population is curated rather than a random survey of forest cover. Disturbance campaigns, geography, acquisition opportunities and year can correlate with labels. Spatial grouping limits nearby pair leakage, but broad geographic gradients and campaign differences remain available. We therefore avoid interpreting these metrics as operational precision, map-wide false-alarm rates or performance in Türkiye. A deployment study would need a suitable spatial sampling frame, target-region preprocessing checks, independent labels and a threshold chosen for its application costs.

Several limitations remain. The retained high-confidence binary windows omit ambiguous, mixed and rare disturbances, and selection uses label histories. The primary audit uses one grouping radius and one fold partition; the single-seed radius extension in Section 5.2 is descriptive, and no leave-country-out analysis is possible because the pinned source table carries no country field. Three seeds quantify limited initialization and subset variation. Fixed 40-epoch recipes may undertrain some methods, as the step-matched control demonstrates. Source digital numbers are not independently harmonized across processing baselines here. The bootstrap does not resolve adaptive development. Foundation-model and multimodal baselines such as those motivating this study are not included in the audited comparison; a frozen linear probe on Presto embeddings run as a separate exploration reached macro-F1 0.71 at 20% labels without fine-tuning or the Sentinel-1, climate and elevation inputs that model expects, so it is reported only as a bounded exploratory note, not as a comparison. These limits prevent a general superiority claim, even though every reported fit is directly reproducible from the supplied cohort and code.

A prior engineering ensemble remains available for label-free inference in the accompanying project. Its previously inspected 486-location test is not reused as the main evidential result in this manuscript. Its calibrated ensemble predictions are also distinct from the fixed-threshold, uncalibrated individual recipes audited here. This separation keeps a working demonstration from being mistaken for untouched scientific validation.
7 Conclusion

On the retained DISFOR cohort, masked temporal pretraining improves a 40-epoch supervised Transformer under a 20% label budget, but an optimizer-step-matched supervised control achieves a higher macro-F1 (0.8987 versus 0.8690). Structured masking does not clearly outperform independent-cell masking, and full-label neural results are similar. The declared extensions sharpen this: along the label-budget curve the pretrained Transformer never exceeds the step-matched control, the CNN or, below 20% labels, the random forest, whereas under coarser spatial separation (20 km, one seed) it degrades least and leads. The benefit of masked pretraining in this setting is therefore better described as robustness to geographic shift than as label efficiency, and that description still needs more seeds and independent regions. The transferable lesson is to report geographic structure, label allocation, optimization controls and negative findings together. Independent, sufficiently supported evaluation remains necessary before claiming target-region or operational generalization.
Data and code availability

The source dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/JR-DIGITAL/DISFOR and is cited in [1]. The exact revision is specified in Section 2 and the reproduction package. The accompanying local review package contains the processed cohort, frozen folds and label subsets, all 180 run records, pooled predictions, analysis scripts, environment lock, figures and manuscript source. It retains the upstream EUPL-1.2 license. No public code archive or DOI has yet been assigned; the local package should not be described as a public deposit. Per-cross-fit weight checkpoints were not retained; exact training recipes and seeds allow their regeneration.
